alignments.note: The conjunction is rendered by “And.”
The finite verb licenses the subject pronoun and auxiliary; the lexical verb “tell” is the target head.
The ASV renders the indirect object as bare “thy son,” leaving the preposition without a separate English realization.
The construct noun is rendered by “son.”
The pronominal suffix is rendered by the possessive “thy.”
The preposition is rendered by “in.”
The noun's article has no separate English article because the phrase is rendered with the demonstrative “that.”
The noun is rendered by “day.”
The article and pronoun jointly form the Hebrew demonstrative rendered by the single English word “that”; the pronoun is the source head.
The preposition of לֵאמֹר has no English realization under rule 27.
The infinitive is rendered by “saying.”
The anticipatory subject “It” is supplied by the English cleft; rule 20 licenses the copula but, apart from presentative “there,” not a supplied subject.
The segmented expression בַּעֲבוּר is rendered as the compound predicate “is because of”; the construction supplies “is,” and “because” carries the relational lexeme.
The substantival demonstrative is expanded as “that which,” headed on the demonstrative “that.”
The verb is rendered by “did”; its explicit subject is aligned separately.
The divine name is rendered by “Jehovah.”
The preposition is rendered by “for.”
The pronominal suffix is rendered by “me.”
The temporal preposition before the infinitive is rendered by “when.”
The infinitive is rendered by the phrasal verb “came forth,” headed on “came.”
The infinitive's pronominal suffix supplies its English subject “I.”
The preposition is rendered by the compound English preposition “out of,” headed on “out.”
The place name is rendered by “Egypt.”

review_notes: The ASV recasts בַּעֲבוּר זֶה as the cleft “It is because of that which.” The supplied copula is assigned to the prepositional predicate, while the anticipatory “It” is treated as added because the contract's verbless-clause rule supplies only the copula apart from presentative “there.”
